item.title: ‘Incredible’ – Bill Simmons mocks John Harbaugh after Giants’ loss to Commanders
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images The New York Giants had a good chance to all but secure their place at the top of the NFC East on Thursday night. They went into the game with a 5-2-1 record and a win over the Washington Commanders would have put some distance between themselves and the second-placed Dallas Cowboys. The Giants were leading the tie late on and looked to be heading towards a big win but when all was said and done, the Commanders managed to secure the victory with less than a minute of the game remaining. On the back of their collapse, Bill Simmons has taken to X/Twitter to mock coach John Harbaugh, saying that he did an incredible job ‘figuring out how to get out coached by Dan Quinn’. Simmons tweeted: “Incredible job by John Harbaugh figuring out how to get outcoached by Dan Quinn.” The Dallas Cowboys now have a chance to tie the Giants for wins this Sunday. However, they would have to hand the San Francisco 49ers just their second loss of the 2026/27 NFL season. Meanwhile, the Giants return to action on November 22 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The 6-2 Jaguars are probably a much tougher test than Washington, with the New York outfit potentially set to be left ruing their missed opportunity on Thursday night. item.title: “Made No Sense”: NFL Insider Questions Giants’ Baffling Play-Calling After Heartbreaking Loss to Commanders
item.description: John Harbaugh - OTA Press Conference © Imagn The New York Giants had a chance to strengthen their grip on the NFC East, but a late-game collapse against the Washington Commanders turned Thursday night’s loss into a missed opportunity. Despite holding a 21-17 lead with less than a minute remaining, the Giants gave up a late touchdown and eventually fell 24-21. NFL insider Ari Meirov questioned New York’s decision-making during its final offensive possession. The team tried to make deep passes despite having two timeouts available. “Throwing deep shots with two timeouts made no sense,” Meirov wrote on X, criticizing the Giants’ approach. New York was doing really well earlier, and it even looked like they would win after J.J. McCarthy connected with Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown, giving the Giants a four-point advantage. However, Jayden Daniels responded with Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with just 57 seconds remaining. The Commanders reclaimed the lead, leaving McCarthy and the Giants with one final opportunity. Later, McCarthy’s final deep attempt toward Malik Nabers was intercepted by Rasul Douglas, sealing Washington’s victory. With two timeouts still available, New York had opportunities to use shorter passes and potentially work its way into scoring position. Instead, the decision to attempt deep shots left little room for error. The questionable approach was frustrating, given how well the Giants’ offense had performed early. McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards and a touchdown. Cam Skattebo also contributed two rushing touchdowns . John Harbaugh Reacts After Giants Surrender Late Lead After the defeat, Harbaugh acknowledged that his team played well in several areas but ultimately failed to do enough to secure the win. “We played a pretty good football game too, just not good enough to win the game. We have a good spirit; it’s not one of fear. It’s one of power and courage. We’ll continue fighting,” Harbaugh said. The Giants’ head coach also said that the loss would not change the team’s broader objectives. “It’s a missed opportunity, but like I told the guys – it would’ve been great to win the game, but it doesn’t change our goals or our opportunity going forward. It’s a tough loss. It’s the National Football League; you’re going to lose some games,” added Harbaugh. New York now sits at 5-3-1, with the Commanders improving to 3-5-1 following their divisional victory. The Giants will have little time to dwell on the disappointment, as the Jacksonville Jaguars are waiting for them in Week 11. item.title: The club preparing to play again after the death of a player
item.description: Ezekiel Williams was a "box-to-box midfielder with high energy who was not afraid of a tackle", says Hendon chairman Cyrus Cooper [Hendon FC] "I messaged Ezekiel because we had a midweek cup game and I wanted to check he was still available," says Adam Fisher - manager of non-league Hendon. "There was no reply. Then I found out what had happened." Ezekiel Williams died in hospital on 2 November from head injuries after an incident in Milton Keynes. He was 26. Two men have been charged with murder. Known to friends as 'Zekes' and 'Eze', Williams was well known in non-league circles having played for clubs including Hastings United, Kettering Town and St Ives Town. A midfielder, he joined Hendon in September and had already established himself at his new club as a "humble, unassuming and generous individual with razor-sharp wit". His death has devastated the part-time club based in Kingsbury, north-west London. "Nothing prepares you for something like this," Hendon's chairman Cyrus Cooper tells BBC Sport. "We're all human beings and the club is struggling to come to terms with what has happened." Hendon, who play in the Isthmian League South Central Division - the eighth tier of English football, have not played since Williams died, as players and staff mourn the loss of a popular player. On Saturday, 12 days after his death, they return to action at Bedfont Sports. "Saturday is going to be so hard because Eze is going to be on our minds and what happened to him," Hendon midfielder Tashae Andall-Gibbons tells BBC Sport. "Everyone is distraught. Eze was only 26 and had his whole life ahead of him." Cooper says: "It's going to be the first time the players put their kit on without Ezekiel being there. "I think there are going to be a lot of tears. It's going to be an emotional day for everyone associated with Hendon Football Club." Ezekiel Williams (right) with his brother Omran and sister Shadore [The Williams Family] 'We are all really struggling' Hendon's grieving players have been offered counselling as they attempt to come to terms with the loss of a team-mate who scored in a league game against Jersey Bulls as recently as 24 October. Three days later, Williams - from Ruislip - started the 2-0 home defeat by Egham Town. It would be his last match. "He messaged me the day after to say: 'Gaffer, I'm really sorry I didn't catch you after the game but I'm going away for the weekend to see a relative who is sick'," says Fisher. "He said: 'I won't be at training on Thursday, I will miss the game on Saturday but I'll be back on Monday.' "That was the last I heard from him." Fisher sent Williams a message on the Monday asking about his availability for a London Cup tie against Woodford, which was due to take place a couple of days later. There was no reply. The following day, via social media, he discovered his player had died. "I found out on the Tuesday afternoon and I didn't leave my house until the Friday," he says. "I was shocked and in a daze." item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.title: Dana White condemns Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili’s brawl: ‘Idiots’
item.description: UFC president Dana White has criticised Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili after their brawl in Abu Dhabi, labelling everyone involved “f***ing idiots”. On Wednesday, Nurmagomedov interrupted Dvalishvili during an interview at a hotel, slapping the UFC bantamweight and sparking a mass brawl . In the chaos, Dvalishvili and a friend attempted to fight off Nurmagomedov and several of the PFL champion’s comrades, with Dvalishvili ultimately left badly bloodied. UFC president and CEO Dana White (Reuters) The fracas occurred days before a Real American Freestyle wrestling event , which is set to feature Dvalishvili and Usman’s brother Umar. “What a bunch of f***ing idiots,” said UFC president and CEO White on Thursday, at the UFC 334 pre-fight press conference. “It’s absolutely ridiculous and stupid, and they’re all in jail. That is not a place to go f*** around.” The UFC has been linked to Nurmagomedov – cousin of UFC great Khabib – in recent weeks, with fans speculating that Wednesday’s attack could cost him a place in the promotion. But White said on Thursday: “He’s still under contract [with the PFL]. We’re not talking him right now anyway.” In early 2025, Dvalishvili retained the UFC bantamweight belt by outpointing Usman’s brother Umar, whose only other professional defeat came in August, when he was knocked out by Song Yadong. Merab Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised after being jumped by Usman Nurmagomedov (Merab Dvalishvili/Instagram) In the aftermath of that knockout, Usman entered the cage and appeared to elbow Song as the latter ran around the cage in celebration. However, many viewers deemed the elbow accidental. Also on Thursday, Nurmagomedov’s manager Ali Abdelaziz told MMA Junkie : “I’m truly sorry [about Wednesday’s events]. It’s embarrassing what happened. I hope these young men will get a good lesson. This is something that should not happen again. I don’t think there’s any words I can say to make this better. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

item.title: Chelsea make decision on Xabi Alonso’s future after Sunderland defeat
item.description: Chelsea make decision on Xabi Alonso’s future after Sunderland defeat Chelsea Back Xabi Alonso as January Transfer Plans Take Shape Chelsea have made an early call on Xabi Alonso and, for now, it is a sensible one. According to Football London, the club are unlikely to sack their manager even if Champions League qualification slips away this season. That matters, because the noise has already started after a mixed opening to the campaign. Alonso arrived with more authority than most recent Chelsea coaches. He was given real influence in recruitment and tasked with cleaning up a long list of poor decisions made under BlueCo. Results at the start looked encouraging, with wins over Fulham and Brighton, but the bounce did not last. Chelsea now sit fifth after 10 league games, 11 points behind Arsenal, and the table already tells a clear story. This team is not where it wants to be, and probably not where the ownership expected it to be either. Still, there is no sign of panic. The report says sacking Alonso is “very unlikely,” and internally this is viewed as “the very start of the Alonso era.” That is the key line. Chelsea have churned through managers often enough to know what instability looks like. If they appointed Alonso to reshape the team, then judging him after a handful of fixtures would be short-term nonsense. Photo IMAGO Xabi Alonso Retains Chelsea Backing There is context here too. Chelsea considered other options before making the appointment. Cesc Fabregas stayed at Como, while Andoni Iraola moved to Liverpool after Arne Slot’s exit. Alonso was the choice, and once you make that choice, you either commit or admit you had no plan in the first place. For now, Chelsea are committing. That does not mean standards disappear. Two defeats in the last three league matches have increased scrutiny, and the gap to the top is already uncomfortable. More importantly, Chelsea are closer to the bottom than first place, which is the sort of stat that quickly turns concern into agitation. January Transfer Plans Point to Midfield Priority The club’s next move looks likely to come in the transfer market. Chelsea wanted a central midfielder in the summer and did not get one done before the deadline. That issue has not gone away. Bournemouth’s Alex Scott is reportedly the leading target, with Chelsea seeing him as the preferred replacement for Enzo Fernandez. Martin Zubimendi is another name under discussion. The Arsenal midfielder has seen his standing change under Mikel Arteta, and Chelsea are among the clubs monitoring the situation, along with Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid. Whether that turns into a genuine January move is another matter, but the interest fits the profile of what Chelsea need, control, composure and technical security in midfield. item.title: Pochettino poised to agree two-and-a-half-year Man United contract
item.description: FILE PHOTO - The United States' head coach Mauricio Pochettino reacts during the 2026 FIFA World Cup round of 16 match between the United States and Belgium at Lumen Field (is associated with: «Pochettino poised to agree two-and-a-half-year Man United contract») Dirk Waem/Belga/dpa Manchester United are set to agree a two-and-a-half-year contract with Mauricio Pochettino to succeed Michael Carrick, the Press Association understands. The Athletic first reported a deal until 2029 had been reached with the Argentinian, who signed a contract extension as United States head coach through to 2030 just three months ago. Pochettino is set to take charge of the US’ Concacaf Nations League quarter-final ties against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday before heading to Manchester. United’s first match after the international break will be against Liverpool on November 22. Pochettino’s current employer, US Soccer, is understood to have accepted he is stepping down but the federation will receive $10 million in compensation for him, and a further $2 million for the departure of his coaching team. An announcement regarding Pochettino could come as early as Friday, with the Argentinian set to hold a press conference previewing the Haiti first leg. US Soccer president Cindy Cone and chief executive JT Batson were understood to be travelling to the national team’s base in Atlanta on Thursday in the wake of the Pochettino news. US Soccer is understood to have placed former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola at the top of its wanted list to replace Pochettino, having made several previous attempts to recruit the Spaniard. Pochettino inherits a United side languishing in 18th place, a start which left United’s bosses feeling they had no choice but to dismiss Carrick. The official announcement of the Englishman’s exit came on Thursday, but had been an open secret all week. One early issue for Pochettino to wrestle with could be the future of star United midfielder Bruno Fernandes. The Portuguese is understood to have rejected a second contract offer, as The Athletic first reported, but club insiders view that as a normal part of contract negotiations. The Red Devils also have an option to extend his deal to the summer of 2028, meaning he would not be free to talk to other clubs in January.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Red Wings are now 20 games into their season. That’s helped to keep Detroit close in a lot of games so far this year. However, the team is 3-7 over their last ten games. The Red Wings went from just under a .500 record and two games out of the middle of the pack to dead last in the division in the span of two weeks. item.title: ‘No money needed’ – How Kirk Cousins got No. 8 back from Minnesota Vikings’ Jakobe Thomas
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images Kirk Cousins got his No. 8 jersey back from Jakobe Thomas after his return to the Minnesota Vikings, and the rookie safety spoke about how it went down. Kirk Cousins’ return to the Minnesota Vikings has been one of the most heartwarming stories of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The quarterback is back with the franchise where he has unfinished business, and he will attempt to complete it wearing his old number. Cousins wore No. 8 on his back during his tenure in Minnesota. The quarterback became one of the franchise’s most consistent ever and finished with a 50-37-1 record as a starter. Upon his return though, his number was already taken by another player. He now has it back, and it is a testament to how much respect he still commands within the franchise. Jakobe Thomas calls Kirk Cousins the ‘rightful owner’ of No. 8, says he just wants him to help win games NFL stars have been known to pay players to get their desired number if it is previously claimed on their new team. Direct cash buyouts are common, sometimes going into the hundreds of thousands, depending on the star’s salary and their desire for the number. Gifts and other luxury items are sometimes also traded for these. However, rookie safety Jakobe Thomas has agreed to give Cousins his number without anything in return. He explained why he decided to do that, and it is a great answer. “No money needed,” Thomas said. “I just need him to come here and win games… A lot of fans have his jersey anyway, so they could pull him out of the closet and put him back on. So that’s all it is. Kirko’s got a lot more memories and history in that number than I do, and it’s rightfully his. So I just gave it back to its rightful owner.” That is a phenomenal answer from the 23-year-old, although he is likely to get a gift from Cousins for his gesture regardless. As a rookie, a nice sum of money would actually go a long way for Thomas, but the youngster is aware that this show of respect will earn him a lot of goodwill and love from fans. item.title: Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams
item.description: Ospreys now play home games at St Helen's [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Ospreys say a report they commissioned into Welsh rugby concludes that the proposed cut of four professional clubs to three should not happen. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has said it intends to drop a side by 2028, with the decision made by next summer. With Cardiff and Dragons set to be granted the capital and east licences, Ospreys and Scarlets are competing to be the side in west Wales. Ospreys asked experts at Sheffield Hallam University to look at the issues and they produced the "Welsh rugby data report". That found "the independent analysis of the data does not logically lead to a conclusion that the removal of one professional team in Wales is a strategic move grounded in evidence". Ospreys say they back the need to keep four clubs. The report has not yet been published in full. That will not be done until later this month when it will be sent to the regions and WRU. Why four clubs should be maintained The Ospreys highlight the reasons the report concludes the number of professional clubs in Wales should remain at four. Derbies: The report claims fixtures between the four Welsh clubs generated 48% of league attendances at home games in Wales from 2012 to 2026. With three clubs, those fixtures would fall from 12 derbies a season to six. Players: Removing one team would create what the report calls a "bottleneck", with fewer elite playing opportunities in Wales and a greater risk of more Welsh players moving to clubs outside the country. Wales: The report finds that Wales have recorded higher Six Nations finishes in the seasons when the Welsh clubs have performed well. All four clubs contribute: Over the period, the report records Cardiff with the highest average attendances, Scarlets as the leading club in the European Cup and Dragons with the highest stadium utilisation, alongside the Ospreys' record in the league and in supplying most players to Wales and the British and Irish Lions. What has not been included in great depth in the initial findings are the financial constraints or how keeping four teams can be afforded. The WRU has reported recent losses of £18m and says it has to reduce its spend on professional rugby from £26m to £20m by 2028. The four sides currently receive about £6.5m each. The Ospreys report follows the Keystone report that was commissioned by the WRU, which said it outlined data why Welsh rugby needs to cut a side. item.title: When will Mauricio Pochettino take charge of Manchester United?
item.description: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United manager just three months into the new season with the club sitting 18th in the Premier League table. The Old Trafford hierarchy pulled the trigger on Carrick’s departure on Thursday morning after three days of speculation following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa which proved to be Carrick’s final match in charge. Thoughts now turn to Carrick’s replacement with former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager Mauricio Pochettino the odds on favourite to take over. Pochettino is the current manager of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) but has reportedly reached a verbal agreement with Man United to sign of as their new head coach. Should his appointment be confirmed when will Pochettino officially begin his tenure? Man United’s next match comes on Sunday 22 November when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool . It will arguably be the most difficult start possible for whoever takes over and it is a game United need to take something from or else they risk dropping further into the relegation zone. The current international break would usually provide a new manager with time to train and see the squad in action but Pochettino, should he be given the job, is unlikely to have such a luxury. That is because the United States have two Nations League matches to play on November 14 and 18 during this window and Pochettino is likely to oversee both fixtures. The Argentine is still contracted to US Soccer until the 2030 World Cup though an early departure from his deal feels increasingly likely. United have made contact with US Soccer over paying compensation to release Pochettino with rumoured figures reaching as high a $10m (£7.4m). Mauricio Pochettino is likely to take charge of Man Utd next week if he is appointed as Michael Carrick's successor (AP) Should an agreement be made, Pochettino could, in theory, leave the US before the scheduled games against Haiti in order to spend time with Man United’s squad ahead of the crucial clash at Anfield. In that case he could arrive at Carrington either the same day or a day after being formally announced as the new head coach. That would give him a maximum of nine days to prepare the team if his appointment is confirmed today (Thursday 12 November). The more likelier option is that Pochettino leads the USMNT for their two fixtures with Haiti and reports to Carrington shortly afterwards. In that case, he could be in post at Man United as early as Wednesday 18 November though given the time difference between the US and the UK, Pochettino would arrive late in the afternoon or early evening. Even so, that would give him three full days, Thursday 19, Friday 20 and Saturday 21 to settle into his new environment and have time on the grass with the squad. Whether three days will be enough for the Argentine to inspire a new manager bounce out of United’s playing group remains to be seen.

item.title: Avalanche HC Jared Bednar Gets Honest on Effort After Senators Loss
item.description: Vegas Golden Knights v Colorado Avalanche Getty The Colorado Avalanche lost 4-3 in overtime to the Ottawa Senators after battling back from a 2-0 first-period deficit. Shane Pinto and Tim Stützle gave Ottawa an early two-goal lead, putting Colorado in a difficult position. In the second period, Artturi Lehkonen got the Avalanche on the board to cut the deficit to one. Then, in the third, Parker Kelly tied the game before Gabriel Landeskog gave Colorado a brief lead. However, Drake Batherson scored to even things up again, and Pinto ultimately sealed the Senators’ victory with an overtime goal. After the game, some Avalanche elements spoke to the media about the loss. Among them was head coach Jared Bednar. Below is the full transcript of Bednar ‘s postgame interview . Jared Bednar: Avalanche Showed ‘a Pretty Gutsy Effort’ vs. Senators Question: You found yourselves in a difficult situation heading into the third period, but you scored a couple of power-play goals and a shorthanded goal. How would you assess your special teams performance tonight? Answer: Great. Yeah, I mean, the penalty kill comes up big, kills them all off and gets a shorthanded goal. The power play delivers a couple of times, too, and gets us back in the game and gives us the lead. I liked the effort all the way around. We played a good hockey team. We were also without a couple of horses for half the game, so it was a pretty gutsy effort from our group. I’ll take it. I mean, we weren’t perfect. We made some mistakes, and they cost us. But all in all, we’re pretty happy with the game and what we did. It’s a big point. Q: Scott (Wedgewood) said this was an opportunity to build character. How would you characterize that aspect of the game? A: Well, I don’t judge our team on results alone. You know that about me. I want to see the effort, commitment, and work. There’s a lot of things we can clean up from that game, but this is a competitive league, and that’s what I want to see right now. We’ll keep working on all the other stuff, but that’s where it starts for me. We’ve put together a nice string of games here when it comes to effort, compete level, and commitment to defending. We’ll clean up a couple of mistakes, but I thought this was a good game, especially after some setbacks. It was a good step in the right direction. We gave ourselves a chance to win. It wasn’t perfect, much like our team, but we battled. Q: What’s it like trying to figure out your power-play units and lines without those guys? A: I think we had a good idea of what we were going to do. Sam Malinski was the obvious choice to step in on the second power-play unit on the back end, and we moved a couple of things around. Obviously, it worked with what we did. Hopefully, those guys get back in the lineup soon, but I don’t know what their situations will be like.
